items.q: If ~90% of thoughts are yesterday's, what does repeating one actually become?
items.a: A **belief**, then a hardwired habit, then an **unconscious program**. Accept it as truth and you get the same choice → behavior → experience → emotion, which drives the same thought.

items.q: Why does stopping an unworthy thought feel like an assault?
items.a: The **body is the mind**. A habit is the body knowing better than the brain. Inhibit the thought and it **craves** the old chemistry, then feeds matching thoughts. Unfamiliar is change; familiar is the known self.

items.q: When you look around and nothing in your life has changed yet, what just happened?
items.a: You left the **bleachers**, then used missing evidence as permission to sit down. The environment lags because **you** have not fully changed.

items.q: Why rehearse Zoom, traffic, and the ex before they happen?
items.a: The brain does not know rehearsal from the event. Keep firing and wiring and it **looks like it already happened**, so behavior can match intention when it is hardest.

items.q: Do you wait to feel worthy until life changes?
items.a: **No.** Generate the elevated emotion first. The body believes it is already in the new environment and, in Dispenza's model, **signals genes ahead of the event**. Lack drops; seeking stops.

items.q: What does meditation literally mean here?
items.a: **Become familiar** — with the old self and the new self. Don't get up until you feel it. Then remember the feeling with eyes open (walking meditation).

items.q: Everyone reacts. What is the actual question?
items.a: **How long will you stay?** Stay and you see life through that lens. Ten resets in one hard day is a day worth living. Altered-state texts are the ones you regret.

items.q: What is an emotion, in this model?
items.a: A **record of the past**. Remembering trauma remakes the chemistry as if it is happening. ~50% of the story is not even true — it justifies why you have not changed.

items.q: When is survival useful, and when is it the whole personality?
items.a: Run from the **predator**. Do not leave the alarm on. Chronic survival is addictive and steals energy from **growth and repair**. One good hour cannot outweigh 15–16 programmed hours.

items.q: Why can't you rewrite the program from stress?
items.a: Survival is **mid-to-high beta** — sports car in first gear; attention on body, environment, time. Slow into **alpha** (door opens) and **theta** (hypnotic). Yelling at the computer is not being in it.

items.q: Where does the elevated feeling come from after you sit through the craving?
items.a: **Inside.** Energy to the heart, then the brain (relaxed heart, awake brain). Not a person, a car, or a game. That is when seeking outside stops.

items.q: If you default back to the old self, did you fail?
items.a: No — that is a **program**. Nobody cares how many times you fell off the bicycle if you ride it now. Show up when the scans have not moved: *what about me still has to change?*
